title: Identification of Drivers of Change of the Gulf of Nicoya Ecosystem (Costa Rica)
model_years: 1995–2014 time series; baseline snapshots referenced as 1995 and 2015
loadability_evidence: Underlying raw fisheries data cannot be published by authors. Native model not verified; the accessible paper alone does not establish complete dynamic reconstructability.
documentation_evidence: EwE fitting study with fisheries effort and environmental drivers; model-fitting comparisons and prey/predator interactions documented.
notes: Companion baseline update: Alms & Wolff 2019, The Gulf of Nicoya (Costa Rica) Fisheries System: Two Decades of Change, doi:10.1002/mcf2.10050. Its table labels use 1993/2013, whereas 2020 narrative uses 1995/2015: preserve this discrepancy pending extraction.
quality_rationale: Provisional screening score. A readable source is not evidence of a successfully reconstructed or load-tested Ecopath model. Underlying raw fisheries data cannot be published by authors. Native model not verified; the accessible paper alone does not establish complete dynamic reconstructability.
geometry_method: No defensible digital study boundary located
geometry_note: Published study location identified, but no defensible numeric model-domain bounding box was extracted; exact author boundary remains unresolved.
recommendation: Same Gulf of Nicoya estuarine system, dynamic fisheries/environment assessment.
coverage_note: Same Gulf of Nicoya estuarine system, dynamic fisheries/environment assessment.

The Gulf of Nicoya is a large tropical estuary located on the Paciﬁc coast of Costa
Rica and accounts for the country’s main ﬁsh production. It is increasingly impacted
not only by its ﬁsheries, but also by urbanization, tourism developments, the input
of pollutants from urban centers and agriculture activities in the catchment areas of
large rivers entering the gulf. Similar to other coastal ecosystems, the gulf is particularly
sensitive to short- and long-term changes in the climate, such as the precipitation rate,
Sea Surface Temperature, wind speed and current regimes. While the gulf has been
studied for decades, until now no attempt has been made to combine the analysis of the
